subject: HIPAA discovery: BAA availability, PHI deployment eligibility, and questionnaire kickoff
messages:
From: Emily Wu <emily.wu@medsys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@medsys.com>, IT Security <medsys-it@medsys.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: HIPAA / BAA + deployment options for PHI use

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking the call today — quick follow-up from our side. MedSys is evaluating using Redwood to power an in-app summarization feature that will process limited PHI (patient names, visits, high-level notes). Before we progress we'd like to confirm a few items so we can scope procurement: 

- Can Redwood sign a standard BAA? If yes, does that apply to Hosted API, Dedicated, or only Private deployments?
- What is Redwood's current SOC 2 posture (Type II available?) and can you share evidence or a redacted report?
- We will need to kick off a Vendor Security Questionnaire (I attached our standard spreadsheet). Who on your side should own that and how long does it usually take to get the answers?
- Any constraints on data residency (we require US-only processing) or log retention for audit purposes?

If easier, please point me to a one-pager that outlines which hosting modes are eligible for PHI and the typical timeline for onboarding.

Thanks,
Emily Wu
Sr. PM, Clinical Integrations
MedSys Health

Attachments: MedSys_Vendor_Q.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wu <emily.wu@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA + deployment options for PHI use

Hi Emily — great speaking with you earlier. Summarizing and next steps below so we have a shared record.

Short answers up front:
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA. Our standard BAA applies to Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Hosted API: the multi-tenant public Hosted API is not eligible for PHI processing.
- SOC 2: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (scope: inference platform and control plane). I will share a redacted summary now and arrange access to the full report under an NDA if needed.
- Data residency: US-only processing is supported for Dedicated and Private — we can pin region and control egress paths.
- Logs/audit retention: audit logs and request-level tracing are available for Dedicated/Private; retention windows and export can be negotiated in the contract.

Attachments I am attaching to this thread:
- Redwood_SOC2_TypeII-summary_redacted.pdf (summary + controls map)
- Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.docx (our editable BAA template)
- deployment-options-matrix.xlsx (high-level comparison: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; notes on PHI eligibility)
- Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-MedSys.xlsx (we copied your sheet and pre-filled common answers — please review)

Proposed next steps:
1) You -> confirm MedSys intends to process PHI for production and the expected peak token throughput (we need this for capacity planning).
2) MedSys -> complete the highlighted tabs in the questionnaire and return (we'll route to our security team).
3) Redwood -> security will respond within 3 business days for standard items; deeper evidence requests may take longer.
4) Contract -> Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate redlines for BAA and hosting SOW once both sides agree on hosting mode.

If helpful we can do a short follow-up with our security lead (Karthik) and a dedicated solutions architect to walk the questionnaire. I've tentatively blocked 30 min on Friday afternoon — let me know if that works.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII-summary_redacted.pdf; Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.docx; deployment-options-matrix.xlsx; Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-MedSys.xlsx

From: Emily Wu <emily.wu@medsys.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@medsys.com>, IT Security <medsys-it@medsys.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA + deployment options for PHI use

Thanks, Soojin — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our security team:

- For Dedicated: are the GPUs and data plane logically isolated per-customer (single-tenant pools) or is isolation at the VM/container level on shared hosts? We need to understand "isolation" for our risk assessment.
- Will the SOC 2 evidence include control coverage for key management and encryption-at-rest?
- What are typical timelines: Dedicated onboarding (from SOW to production) vs Private (VPC) deployment?
- Do you have a standard SLA or uptime commitment for Dedicated customers that handle PHI?

We will start completing the questionnaire and aim to return it by next Wed. Also, confirm: if we decide to proceed, who will be our primary Redwood contact for technical onboarding?

Best,
Emily

Attachment: completed_questionnaire_stub.xlsx (we will send full when done)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wu <emily.wu@medsys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA + deployment options for PHI use

Hi Emily — quick answers inline and next steps.

- Isolation: For Dedicated customers processing PHI we provide single-tenant GPU pools (reserved capacity) so the inference runtime and KV caches are dedicated to your tenancy. The control plane is logically separated and access-controlled; we document network boundaries in the SOW. For highest isolation we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) where customer-controlled networking is enforced.
- SOC 2 evidence: the redacted summary covers encryption, KMS integration, key lifecycle controls, and separation of duties. Full supporting evidence (under NDA) includes control mappings for KMS usage and encryption-at-rest procedures.
- Timelines: Dedicated onboarding typically 4–6 weeks after SOW sign (depends on capacity and config). Private/VPC deployments are typically 6–10 weeks (networking and customer IT approvals often drive cadence).
- SLA: Dedicated customers can opt into SLA-backed tiers. For PHI workloads we recommend the SLA tier that includes 99.9% uptime and a defined NIST-aligned incident response playbook; Marissa will scope this in the commercial term sheet.

Primary technical contact: Karthik (cc'd) — he will run the onboarding and introduce the solutions architect and security reviewer.

Next actions for both sides:
1) MedSys: return the completed questionnaire (we annotated common fields already).
2) Soojin/Marissa: set up a security review call with Karthik and MedSys IT — propose Tue 6/16 10:00am PT (please confirm).
3) Marissa: prepare initial commercial SOW with Dedicated + Private options and draft SLA language.

I will attach the redacted SOC summary and the editable BAA in a follow-up email for Legal to start redlines. Appreciate the quick turnaround on the questionnaire — once we have that we can commit to the security review slot.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII-summary_redacted.pdf; Redwood_BAA_Draft_v1.docx
